text:
alice: Hey team — after we rotated the OAuth client for Okta last night a few users report they can no longer open Project 'zephyr' in the console. They see a 403 / permission denied when switching orgs. Happens for web console only; API keys work. Repro steps I have below. 

jordan: Thanks — can you paste a repro? which users, and are they SSO users or local? :thinking_face:

alice: SSO users only (Okta). Steps:
```
1) Login to console via Okta SSO
2) Click org dropdown -> switch to Project zephyr
3) Console shows "Permission denied" overlay, buttons grayed out
4) curl with API key to projects endpoint returns 200
```

sam: Can you paste the network/fetch console log or the response body for the 403? sometimes the auth cookie gets cleared after client rotations.

alice: Copied response from network tab:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "message": "missing_role_claim: user does not have project access"
}
```

security-bot: Notifying security on-call due to auth claim anomaly. :rotating_light: @security

security-bot: Known issue: if IdP client rotation omits or renames the role/group claim, users will authenticate but role mapping fails.

jordan: @alice can you confirm whether the Okta app's assertion/claim mapping changed? specifically the `roles` or `groups` claim name or transform?

emily: I ran a quick check — Okta admin console shows the app still sends `groups`, but there is a new transformation rule applied during rotation that trims prefix `org:` from groups. Could that break mapping?

sam: Yes — our console expects group names like `org:acme:zephyr-admins`. If Okta now sends `acme:zephyr-admins` the SCIM/claim matcher will not match and RBAC will drop project role. That explains why API keys (which use internal bindings) still work.

jordan: Workaround: re-add the original group claim mapping in Okta or create a temporary mapping rule to reintroduce `org:` prefix. Alternatively, log in and force a full session refresh for the affected users (logout -> clear cookies -> login) — will pick up any updated claims but won't help if claim content was transformed.

alice: Customer wants a quick fix. Do we have a server-side hotfix that relaxes the claim matcher to accept both prefixed and unprefixed group names?

sam: We can deploy a tolerant matcher as a short-term change: treat `acme:zephyr-admins` as equivalent to `org:acme:zephyr-admins` for role resolution. Low-risk patch, but needs canary and rollback plan. I'll open a tiny change and request a canary rollout to dedicated infra.

dev_prod: Small note: watch for collisions if different orgs share the same unprefixed group name. Prefixing is deliberate. We'll add telemetry for ambiguous matches.

jordan: In the meantime, support steps to give to customer: 
- Confirm Okta group claim name + transformations
- If feasible, revert the transformation so group values keep `org:` prefix
- For immediate access: add the user to a console project role (temporary) via support admin panel or provide a service token (scope: project:read)

alice: I applied the Okta temporary mapping for 3 affected groups and asked users to logout/login. Two users report access restored. One user still blocked — investigating session caching.

emily: Confirmed — logout/login fixed it for me. Thanks! :tada:

jordan: Follow-ups:
- sam to ship tolerant matcher canary (P0 -> canary within 2hrs)
- security to review claim transform policy for rotations
- docs: update Okta rotation checklist with a step to preserve role/group claim naming

sam: Filing PR and canary now. Tracking id: INF-4921. Will post status in this thread when canary is up.

alice: Thanks all — I'll keep the customer updated.

emily: One question — will this affect audits? we had a rotation noted in our change log.

jordan: Good call. security will annotate the rotation event and the mitigation steps so audit trail is preserved.

sam: Canary deployed to 10% of traffic. Monitoring keys: error-rate, ambiguous-match-rate. No regression in 12m. Increasing canary to 50%.

alice: Customer confirmed full fix after canary reached 50% and Okta mapping reverted. Closing the loop. :white_check_mark:
